Click the file on GitHub and click 'Raw' to copy the raw.githubusercontent.com URL. 4. Paste that URL into Static Polling Manifest URL before exporting your release .zip.
edge_guide_lineage_how_desc: Sanctuary OS identifies {mods} by cryptographic SHA-256 DNA rather than fragile filenames. Every exported manifest.json tracks three hash layers so updates and multi-file suites never break:
edge_guide_lineage_how_title: How Lineage Hash Tracking Works Under the Hood
edge_guide_lineage_layer1_desc: Records the primary .package hash plus every sibling .package and .ts4script module in the current release. All sibling modules in a multi-file suite (like MCCC) are recognized as current and grouped under a single parent folder card.
edge_guide_lineage_layer2_desc: Every time you click Export Static Manifest (.zip) over an existing Sandbox folder (or add historical hashes in Details & Versions), prior release hashes are rolled into previous_hashes. When Sanctuary OS polls your remote manifest.json, any {Citizen} whose installed file matches a hash in previous_hashes immediately receives an Update Available badge.
edge_guide_lineage_layer3_desc: When a {Citizen} drops your new v1.1.0 .zip into Sanctuary OS, the ingestion engine checks their installed {Vault} against previous_hashes. Even if you renamed MyMod_v1.0.package to MyMod_v1.1.package, Sanctuary OS finds the old v1.0 file by its lineage hash and replaces it in-place inside the exact same subfolder—preventing duplicate {mod} collisions.
edge_guide_lineage_rules_desc: In Rules & Upload, dependencies and conflicts can reference other {mods} by SHA-256 hash, Registry UUID, or plain {mod} name (e.g., 'XML Injector'). Sanctuary OS resolves both object rules and plain string names automatically.
edge_guide_lineage_rules_title: Flexible Dependency & Conflict Matching (Hash or Name)
edge_guide_step1_desc: Drop your .package, .ts4script, and optional .cfg/.ini files into Dev/Sandbox (or click Import in the {Mason} Workshop). Open the {mod} card and configure its Details & Versions (Name, {Mason} Version, Safety Tier 0–4, Game Versions), Files & Folders (Twin scripts, Add-on modules, Folder Structure), and Rules & Upload (Required DLC, Dependencies, and Severity 3–4 Conflicts).
edge_guide_step2_desc: Paste the raw URL where your manifest.json (single {mod}) or catalog.json (all your {mods} in one file) will live—such as GitHub Raw, Cloudflare Pages, GitLab Raw, or your own website. Sanctuary OS embeds this URL directly into both manifest.json and override.json inside your release .zip.
edge_guide_step3_desc: Click Export Static Manifest (.zip) in Rules & Upload (or the top-right inbox icon). Sanctuary OS computes the SHA-256 hash of every file in your release, writes manifest.json and override.json into your Sandbox folder, and bundles {ModName}_v{Version}_SanctuaryRelease.zip. Upload the .zip to your download page (Patreon, Itch.io, CurseForge, SFS) and push manifest.json to your static URL.
edge_guide_step4_desc: When releasing v1.1.0+, place the updated .package/.ts4script files into the same Sandbox folder, bump the {Mason} Version field, and click Export Static Manifest (.zip) again. Sanctuary OS automatically reads your previous manifest.json and SQLite history, rolls the old v1.0.0 SHA-256 hashes into previous_hashes (archive_hashes), and records the new hashes as current_hashes. Replace manifest.json on your static host—every {Citizen} on v1.0.0 will automatically get an Update Available alert!
edge_guide_step5_desc: A {Citizen} drags your release .zip into Sanctuary OS once. With zero confirmation popups, Sanctuary OS registers your manifest_url and lineage hashes in SQLite, marks the {mod} STABLE, groups multi-file suites into a single parent card, enforces your DLC/Dependency/Conflict rules, alerts them when you update manifest.json, and replaces old files in-place (even if renamed) when they drop the new .zip.

schema_doc_scan_paths_desc: Default Steam, EA App, Origin, Epic, GOG, and macOS /Applications paths checked automatically during workspace setup.
schema_doc_tc_engine_desc: Core game binary folders (relative to the game installation root) archived during Engine State {Backups} snapshots.
schema_doc_tc_world_desc: User data folders and settings files (relative to user_data_dir) archived during World State {Backups} snapshots.
schema_doc_tiers_desc: Defines the load order tiers available to {Citizens}. Higher Priority Weight tiers win resource conflicts over lower tiers.
schema_doc_ver_file_desc: Relative path to the file storing the installed game patch string and the regex pattern used to extract it, with Windows Registry and macOS Plist fallbacks.
